why.3: An evening when you change the menu because there is no time to make broth. The ingredients you bought stay as they are, and only tonight's pot of soup disappears.
why.4: Dak-hanmari Broth is the soup base that fills that gap. Add the chicken and vegetables as they are; only the work of making the broth is in the bottle.

gaps.3: We've listed the points that often give people pause when choosing a soup base, using the label and verified information.
gaps.4: I don't know how much water to add
gaps.6: Use 50g of soup base (about a quarter of a paper cup) with 450g of water (two and a half paper cups). For a lighter soup, 500g of water; for a stronger one, 400g of water — keep the amount of soup base the same and adjust only the water.
gaps.7: Ratio recommended by the manufacturer's researcher
gaps.8: I can't tell how far one bottle goes
gaps.9: We wrote down the size and number of uses in advance.
gaps.10: The bottle is 6cm wide and deep and 18cm tall, and holds 330g. 1 use is 50g, so one bottle gives 6 uses with 30g left. Each use is 2 servings, so 6 uses make 12 servings.
gaps.11: I thought it had chicken, like in the photo
gaps.13: Chicken, potatoes, Korean chives and green onion are ingredients you add and boil yourself, to taste. The label lists chicken 2.7%, chicken extract 0.1% and chicken fat 0.1%.
gaps.15: What if the taste isn't as expected?
gaps.17: It has a deep, clean flavor extracted from Korean-origin chicken. The ingredients include chicken breast from Korea, concentrated beef-bone extract and L-glutamic acid sodium salt (flavor enhancer). It is already seasoned, so taste it at the end and decide on salt then.
gaps.18: Full ingredients in label info below
gaps.19: What about the use-by date and storage?
gaps.20: Use-by date and storage, in one place.
gaps.21: The use-by date is 12 months from the date of manufacture (room temperature), and the exact date is marked on the container. Before opening, store it in a cool place away from direct sunlight. After opening, seal it, refrigerate it and use it quickly.
gaps.23: Is the sediment at the bottom okay?
gaps.24: It's a soup base you shake before use.
gaps.25: Layers may separate and sediment may form because of the nature of the raw materials, but quality is not affected. Shake well before use.
how.7: Layers may separate and sediment may form because of the nature of the raw materials, but quality is not affected. Shake the bottle up and down well to mix it evenly.
how.9: This is for 2 servings. 50g of soup base is about a quarter of a paper cup, and 450g of water is two and a half paper cups (based on a 180ml paper cup). Adjust the amount to your taste.
how.11: Add the chicken, potatoes, Korean chives and green onion, then boil.
how.12: Add ingredients to your taste and boil, and you have a pot of dak-hanmari (Korean whole-chicken pot): soup for two. Juk (rice porridge) gets more concentrated as it reduces, so add water to adjust.
calc.3: These are calculated values that scale the 2-serving ratio (50g soup base + 450g water) up or down as is. Strength changes only the water; the amount of soup base stays the same.

calc.15: The gram amounts for each group size are calculated by scaling the ratio for 2 servings, so adjust the amount to your taste. Weighing on a scale is the most accurate way.

faq.3: How many times can I use one bottle?
faq.4: 1 use is 50g, so one bottle gives 6 uses with 30g left. Each use is 2 servings, so 6 uses make 12 servings.
faq.6: For 2 servings, 50g of soup base + 450g of water is the ratio recommended by the manufacturer's researcher. To taste, adjust the water between 500g (lighter) and 400g (stronger).
faq.7: Is there chicken in it too?
faq.8: The bottle contains soup base. Add chicken, potatoes, Korean chives, green onion and other ingredients yourself, to taste, and boil. The label lists chicken 2.7%, chicken extract 0.1% and chicken fat 0.1%.
faq.9: Do I need to add more salt or soy sauce?
faq.10: The product is already seasoned. After boiling, taste it at the end and add only a very small amount if needed.
faq.11: The bottle has separated layers and sediment.
faq.12: Layers may separate and sediment may form because of the nature of the raw materials, but quality is not affected. Shake well before use.
faq.13: How should I store it after opening?
faq.14: Seal it, refrigerate it and use it quickly. Before opening, store it at room temperature (1℃~35℃) in a cool place away from direct sunlight.
faq.16: Contains soy, wheat, milk, chicken and beef. Products that use eggs, buckwheat, peanuts, crab, shrimp, mackerel, pork, peach, tomato, sulfites, walnuts, squid, shellfish and pine nuts are also made in the same facility.
final.3: 50g of soup base, 450g of water, one whole chicken. With just salt, pepper and seasoned Korean chives on the side, it makes a full meal.
